protocol: Indian Air Force preconversion chamber test in New Delhi. A ground-to-5,000-ft ear-clearance check preceded staged ascent to 37,000 ft. The chamber record describes high-flow oxygen and use of emergency oxygen after symptom onset. Prebreathe length and actual delivered oxygen fraction were unavailable.
outcome_window: First new symptoms at the 51st minute at 37,000 ft. Symptoms improved on descent, with recurrent hypotension at 14:30. Asymptomatic the following morning and discharged on 12 June.
locator: Case History, Chamber Record and Discussion, printed pp. 10–13
note: The model uses the existing review observation for one case. The scan on p. 10 dates the chamber test 5 June 1957. The 6 June entry on p. 12 is the first documented asymptomatic examination. Hospital discharge recorded DCS. The proposed pulmonary vascular mechanism was unconfirmed. The paper provides no population denominator or staff comparator.
